title: Understanding doubly robust methods
text: Suppose outcome whether patient relapse one year. want population-average risk difference: proportion relapse everyone received treatment 1 minus proportion relapse everyone received treatment 0. negative difference means fewer relapses treatment 1. marginal effect distinct treatment effect conditional particular patient’s covariates. observational data, observed difference relapse proportions may reflect differences baseline characteristics well treatment. Two approaches can help adjust measured covariates: Inverse probability weighting (IPW) uses treatment model estimate patient’s propensity score: probability receiving treatment 1 given covariates. Patients receive weight received treatment less likely given covariates. weighted relapse outcomes compared treatment groups. Propensity scores can also used matching, stratification, regression adjustment; see Chapter 7 introduction methods (Jiang et al. 2026). Outcome-model standardization, also called g-computation, uses outcome model predict relapse given treatment covariates. patient target population, model predicts probability relapse treatment 0 treatment 1, using patient’s observed covariates. Averaging predictions separately treatment gives two estimated population-average risks; difference estimates risk difference. example, average predicted risks 20% treatment 0 15% treatment 1 give risk difference -5 percentage points. approaches need causal identification assumptions, including well-defined treatments consistency, unmeasured treatment–outcome confounding given adjustment covariates, positivity: treatment must possible relevant covariate values. also need suitable modeling regularity assumptions. Outcome-model standardization generally relies correctly specified outcome model, whereas IPW relies correctly specified treatment model. sometimes called singly robust approaches respect model misspecification.

title: Understanding doubly robust methods
text: following synthetic example compares three estimates population-average risk difference, treatment 1 minus treatment 0, relapse within one year. Now fit doubly robust AIPW estimator atefit(). cate.model specifies outcome covariates; atefit() adds treatment , default, treatment–covariate interactions. ps.model specifies treatment model. 50 bootstrap replicates keep example quick; use substantive analysis examine bootstrap diagnostics. estimates need agree finite sample, even necessary assumptions hold. displayed confidence interval applies atefit() estimate, two illustrative calculations. confidence interval describes sampling uncertainty procedure; account unmeasured confounding establish either model correct.
code: library(precmed) dat <- simulate_binary(n = 4000, seed = 2026, followup = 1, threshold = 0) table(dat$trt) #>  #> drug0 drug1  #>  1858  2142 outcome_fit <- glm(y ~ trt * (age + previous_treatment),                    data = dat, family = binomial()) treatment_fit <- glm(trt ~ age + previous_treatment,                      data = dat, family = binomial())  under_0 <- under_1 <- dat under_0$trt <- factor("drug0", levels = levels(dat$trt)) under_1$trt <- factor("drug1", levels = levels(dat$trt)) standardized <- mean(predict(outcome_fit, under_1, type = "response")) -   mean(predict(outcome_fit, under_0, type = "response"))  # Match the default propensity-score limits used by atefit(). ps <- pmin(pmax(predict(treatment_fit, type = "response"), 0.01), 0.99) treated <- dat$trt == "drug1" ipw <- mean(treated * dat$y / ps) - mean((!treated) * dat$y / (1 - ps)) fit <- atefit(response = "binary", data = dat,               cate.model = y ~ age + previous_treatment,               ps.model = trt ~ age + previous_treatment,               n.boot = 50, seed = 999) c(outcome_standardization = standardized, ipw = ipw,   doubly_robust = unname(fit$risk.difference$estimate)) #> outcome_standardization                     ipw           doubly_robust  #>             -0.10298071             -0.09978176             -0.10762720 confint(fit) #>                      2.5 %      97.5 % #> risk.difference -0.1421899 -0.07306452

Propensity score truncation can affect guarantee based treatment model. AIPW risk estimates need lie [0, 1]. Outcomes fully observed intended follow-horizon; function adjust censoring. bootstrap replicate refits models. replicate risk difference fails non-finite, inference unavailable; failures summarized warning stored bootstrap.diagnostics. diagnostics() can used inspect records. point estimate standard error returned coef() result object; confint() calculates Wald intervals requested level.

title: Cross-validation of the conditional average treatment effect (CATE) score — catecv
text: binary outcomes, iteration randomly splits treatment arm training validation sets. score fitted training data applied sets. Percentile cutoffs calculated separately set using scores, without using validation outcomes. Ties may make nested groups larger nominal proportions. Mutually exclusive groups use half-open intervals, last interval including upper endpoint; tied cutoffs can produce empty groups. Subgroup risk differences estimated separately set using augmented inverse-propensity estimator. Score-fitting subgroup failures return NA warning recorded diagnostics; ABC NA required estimate unavailable. ABC integrates validation risk-difference curve minus overall validation effect, reversing sign lower outcomes desirable. subgroup comparisons assess ranking, calibration; causal interpretation requires exchangeability, positivity, consistency, appropriate nuisance-model assumptions. error.max max.iter supported binary splits. binary score methods described catefit(). count response, see details catecvcount(). survival response, see details catecvsurv(). continuous response, see details catecvmean().

title: Cross-validation of the conditional average treatment effect (CATE) score for count outcomes — catecvcount
text: CATE score represents individual-level treatment effect expressed rate ratio count outcomes. can estimated boosting, Poisson regression, negative binomial regression, doubly robust estimator two regressions (Yadlowsky, 2020) applied separately treatment group doubly robust estimator contrast regression (Yadlowsky, 2020) applied entire data set. Internal CV applied reduce optimism choosing CATE estimation method captures treatment effect heterogeneity. CV applied repeating following steps cv.n times: Split data training validation set according train.prop.  training validation sets must balanced respect covariate distributions  doubly robust rate ratio estimates (see error.max). Estimate CATE score training set specified scoring method. Predict CATE score validation set using scoring model fitted  training set. Build nested subgroups treatment responders training validation sets,  separately, estimate ATE within nested subgroup. element  prop.cutoff (e.g., prop.cutoff[] = 0.6), take following steps: Identify high responders observations 60%    (.e., prop.cutoff[]x100%) highest (higher.y = TRUE)    lowest (higher.y = FALSE) estimated CATE scores. Estimate ATE subgroup high responders using doubly robust estimator. Conversely, identify low responders observations 40%    (.e., 1 - prop.cutoff[]x100%) lowest (higher.y = TRUE)    highest (higher.y = FALSE) estimated CATE scores. Estimate ATE subgroup low responders using doubly robust estimator. abc = TRUE, calculate area ATE series ATEs  nested subgroups high responders validation set. Build mutually exclusive subgroups treatment responders training  validation sets, separately, estimate ATE within subgroup. Mutually exclusive  subgroups built splitting estimated CATE scores according prop.multi.

title: precmed 1.1.0.9000 (development version)
text: Added support binary outcomes risk-difference scale atefit(), catefit(), catecv(), including doubly robust estimation, logistic boosting scores, cross-validated subgroup estimates, new vignette. Binary cross-validation uses treatment-stratified splits rather balanced-split controls error.max max.iter. Standardized bootstrap failure handling across binary, count survival atefit(): affected measures now unavailable inference replicate fails undefined, instead silently omitting count replicates. Results record replicate-level reasons bootstrap.diagnostics diagnostics(). Added population-level log.cumulative.hazard.ratio tau0 survival atefit(), bootstrap inference. Inference unavailable estimate bootstrap replicate undefined. replaces conditional Cox log.hazard.ratio atefit() output, breaking change. Subgroup validation conditional HR outputs remain available hr.*; values can change horizon correction described . Added subgroup cumulative hazard ratios survival catefit() catecv() chr.* outputs; hr.* outputs remain conditional Cox hazard ratios. Survival plots box plots now accept measure = "rmtl" (default), "cumulative_hr", "conditional_hr"; validation curves can display multiple measures. previously supported plot.hr argument deprecated; plot.hr = TRUE now selects cumulative hazard ratio default rather conditional Cox HR. Use measure = "conditional_hr" plot latter. Older saved objects must refitted cumulative hazard plots. Added C backends, enabled default, count survival contrast regression, Cox restricted mean survival integration, LASSO propensity-score interaction screening. Installing source now requires C compiler R’s standard BLAS/LAPACK libraries. Added contrast.control, rmst.control, ps.control numerical backend settings. Set solver = "R" use R implementation; small floating-point differences backends possible. Replaced gbm gbm3 boosting models. Existing tuning argument names learning rate 0.1 preserved; stored fits now class GBMFit. Results can differ even identical settings random seeds. Added simulate_count(), simulate_binary(), simulate_survival() generate reproducible synthetic data illustrating testing package’s methods confounding heterogeneous treatment effects.

title: precmed 1.1.0.9000 (development version)
text: Exported catefitbinary() binary-outcome counterpart catefitcount() catefitsurv(), dedicated help page. Expanded catefit() help compare CATE score methods explain use doubly robust estimation qualifications. Added package-level overview accessible ?precmed, including short example, effect scales, links online guides handbook. Added introductory vignette explaining doubly robust estimation, propensity score weighting, outcome-model standardization (g-computation), assumptions, use precmed. Added subgroup_estimates() extract nested binary, count survival subgroup estimates scoring method measure. Newly fitted survival catefit() objects also retain subgroup treatment-specific risks RMSTs risk differences. Added predict(), coef() confint() methods catefit score extraction. Predictions return stored analysis-sample scores; coefficient intervals require available contrast-regression standard errors available survival fits. Survival atefit() bootstrap plots group RMST, risks cumulative hazard ratio row default; metrics still controls selection order accepts underscore spellings dotted metric names. Survival catecv() now stores subgroup risk differences tau0; validation plots support measure = "risk_difference"; dotted measure names available aliases. Survival atefit() now reports treatment-specific event risks difference tau0, bootstrap inference plot support. diagnostics(fit, type = "propensity") now reports full-sample propensity score overlap, truncation, inverse treatment weights effective sample sizes newly fitted binary, count survival atefit() results. default message table unchanged. Overlap diagnostics now default compact formatted table; use layout = "arms" layout = "metrics" unrounded numeric results; type = "overlap" remains alias. Binary atefit() bootstrap plots now display treatment-specific risks risk difference default. metrics selects orders risk0, risk1, risk.difference. Older objects without risk bootstrap estimates retain risk-difference plot. Added plot() support catefit score distributions, histograms, optional density curves, method selection, configurable reference line. score axis uses original treatment labels available; newly fitted catefit objects retain labels, older fits use treatment 0/1. Binary, count survival vignettes now use method. binary vignette compares logistic two-regression scores internal validation splits, uses 10 iterations larger subgroups reduce rank-deficient fits, removes redundant manual validation example, explains printed average treatment effect showing extraction plotting commands. Standardized documentation terminology outcome, treatment censoring models, clarifying propensity scores inverse probability censoring weights. Clarified binary, count survival outcome support package description, README, quick start function documentation. README introductory vignettes also describe survival risk differences distinguish scale survival CATE scores. quick start presents estimated count rate ratio confidence interval concise table. Added ATE methods vignette covering binary, count survival outcomes, assumptions bootstrap inference; CATE methods vignette separates score development validation. Added combine abc() aggregate cross-validation iterations per scoring method mean, median, user-supplied function. default still returns full matrix; missing values removed automatically. Added dashed null reference line count survival atefit() bootstrap log-ratio plots. null.value defaults 0 log scale can set another value, NULL, NA; treatment-specific RMST panels unchanged. Count atefit() now retains bootstrap rate estimates treatment labels; bootstrap plot displays rates treatments alongside log rate ratio. Older saved fits continue display log-ratio panel . Added metrics plot.atefit() select order available bootstrap metrics names fitted object. Improved bootstrap histogram styling minimal default theme panel headings, added caption explaining estimate null reference lines. Supply theme use another ggplot2 theme. Histogram bars now default alpha = 1 background grid show . Applied default theme validation curves subgroup box plots; theme argument still accepts custom ggplot2 theme. Captions explain dashed overall treatment effect reference lines. Multi-measure survival plots use horizontal panel headings matched y scales within measure. Set show.overall = FALSE validation curves box plots hide overall effect line. Validation curves accept layout = "method" compare training validation curves within method-specific panels. Subgroup box plots now default two columns; ncol controls layout. Validate outcome types outcome-specific CATE scoring methods fitting, including empty invalid inputs. Added catecvCountExample, pre-fitted validation result used ABC plotting examples avoid repeatedly fitting models. Label survival atefit() bootstrap plot panels original treatment names available, use readable names treatment effects. Report automatic treatment recoding informational message rather warning, retaining mapping existing result objects. Added diagnostics() summarize recorded survival atefit() treatment recoding information subgroup errors warnings catefit() catecv() results data frame. Added coef() confint() methods extracting supported treatment effects confidence intervals count survival atefit() results. Improved performance balanced splitting, continuous contrast regression, censoring probability calculations, propensity-score LASSO fitting. Updated validation plots box plots current ggplot2 tidyselect versions; ggplot2 >= 3.4.0 now required. Added book chapter Jiang et al. (2026) package description references. Added Smart Data Analysis Statistics B.V. copyright holder contributions version 1.1.0, alongside existing Biogen attribution.
